metaDescription: 18V cordless tool batteries compared by amp-hours, platform breadth, fuel gauges and cell design for Milwaukee M18, Makita LXT and Ryobi ONE+ tools.
expertTake: The Milwaukee M18 REDLITHIUM 5.0Ah is the best 18V battery for most professionals because of its onboard fuel gauge, REDLINK protection and the largest 18V tool line. The Makita BL1850B 5.0Ah is the pick for LXT users who want a 45 minute charge. The Ryobi ONE+ HP 4.0Ah is the value pick with a very broad tool lineup. Packs only fit their own platform, so buy into a system, not just a capacity.
introParagraphs: A cordless tool battery is a pack of lithium cells in series with a small circuit board that watches temperature, voltage and current. That board is why a good pack shuts off before it overheats, and why a tool and a pack from the same maker work better together.
Capacity, protection electronics and platform breadth decide which pack is worth owning.

products.name: Milwaukee 48-11-1850 M18 REDLITHIUM 5.0Ah Battery
products.description:
The 48-11-1850 is a 5.0Ah M18 REDLITHIUM pack with REDLINK Intelligence, which uses communication between the tool, battery and charger to optimize performance and give overload protection. An onboard fuel gauge shows remaining runtime.

The communication system is the reason Milwaukee tools last: the pack and tool exchange data, so the tool can throttle before the pack overheats. M18 is also the broadest 18V professional platform, with more than 60 compatible tools according to a Milwaukee listing for a related pack. A 5.0Ah capacity is about 90 watt-hours, enough for a day of drilling and a half day of cutting.

Compared with the Makita BL1850B, the Milwaukee has stronger system communication and a wider tool range. Keep the pack out of extreme heat and store it partly charged. Keep a charger on the truck dash or bench so the pack never sits flat, and rotate two packs so neither ages faster.
products.bestFor: Professionals and serious DIYers on the M18 platform.
pros: REDLINK Intelligence protects pack and tool
Fits the broadest M18 tool line
cons: Ties you to the M18 platform

products.name: Milwaukee M18 REDLITHIUM XC5.0 Resistant Battery

specList.label: Housing
specList.value: Resistant to common oils and chemicals

products.description:
The XC5.0 Resistant battery is a 5.0Ah M18 pack in a housing designed to protect against common oils and chemicals. It is the same capacity class as the standard 48-11-1850, with a tougher shell.

The resistant housing matters in shops, garages and industrial sites, where solvents and oil degrade ordinary plastic and cause cracks. The internals are the usual REDLITHIUM cells and REDLINK electronics. The extra protection costs more than a standard pack.

Choose it if your packs live in a truck with oil and cleaners. For a clean home shop, the standard pack is enough. Wipe the pack with a damp cloth after shop days and check the terminals for pitting, since oily grime on contacts can cause connection problems.
products.bestFor: Garage, shop and industrial users around oils and chemicals.
pros: Resistant housing guards against oils and chemicals
cons: Costs more than the standard pack
Little benefit in a clean home shop

products.name: Makita BL1850B 18V LXT 5.0Ah Battery

specList.label: Runtime claim
specList.value: Up to 65 percent more than BL1830 (maker)

products.description:
The BL1850B is a 5.0Ah LXT battery with an LED charge level indicator that Makita says charges fully in 45 minutes or less and gives up to 65 percent more runtime than the 3.0Ah BL1830. The 65 percent claim compares two Makita packs, which is simple math on capacity.

A 45 minute charge on a rapid charger means one pack can be swapped and recharged while the other works. The LXT platform covers hundreds of tools, from drills to mowers, and the batteries share between them. Compared with the Milwaukee M18 pack, the Makita lacks a fuel gauge on the pack itself, relying on LEDs, but charges quickly.

Store it cool and keep the contacts clean. It is a dependable choice for LXT owners. Use it with a rapid charger to get the 45 minute figure, because a slow charger will take much longer.
products.bestFor: LXT users who want a fast-charging 5.0Ah pack.
pros: Fits the huge LXT tool range

products.name: Makita BL1850B-2 18V LXT 5.0Ah Battery 2-Pack
products.description:
The BL1850B-2 is a two-pack of 5.0Ah LXT batteries with the same LED indicator and 45 minute charge time as the single pack. Two packs let you run a tool while charging the other.

Buying a pair is the practical way to avoid downtime. Each pack stores about 90 watt-hours, so two packs give roughly 180 watt-hours between charges. A pair also averages the wear, since you can alternate them. They suit a saw or a grinder that drains a single pack in an hour.

Rotate the packs so each ages evenly, and label them if you want to track age. Charge both before a long job. Mark the packs 1 and 2 with a paint pen and swap which one goes in first each day, so wear stays even across both.
products.bestFor: LXT users who work all day and need a spare.
pros: Full charge in 45 minutes or less
cons: Costs more than a single pack
Same pack is not compatible outside LXT

products.name: Ryobi PBP004 ONE+ High Performance 4.0Ah Battery

specList.label: Power claim
specList.value: Up to 30 percent more than standard (maker)

products.description:
The PBP004 is a 4.0Ah ONE+ High Performance pack. Ryobi says it provides up to 30 percent more power than standard lithium and runs longer, comparing against its own earlier packs. More than 225 ONE+ tools accept it.

The ONE+ platform is the broadest home platform, covering drills, mowers, vacuums and lights, so one pack serves the whole house. High Performance packs use better cells that can deliver current to brushless tools. A 4.0Ah pack stores about 72 watt-hours.

It is the budget-friendly way into a big platform. Compared with the Milwaukee, it targets homeowners rather than professionals, and the build is less rugged. Because it is a High Performance pack, pair it with brushless ONE+ tools to see the benefit; on basic drills a standard pack does the same job.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who run many ONE+ tools.
pros: High Performance cells for brushless tools
cons: Maker's power claims compare against its own old packs

products.name: Ryobi ONE+ 18V 2.0Ah Battery and Charger Kit
products.description:
This is a 2.0Ah ONE+ battery and charger kit with a claim of extreme weather performance and a charge time under an hour. Ryobi says it delivers up to 1.5 times more runtime than earlier standard packs.

A 2.0Ah pack stores about 36 watt-hours, so it suits drills, drivers and light tools more than saws. A kit with a charger is the cheapest way to start on the ONE+ platform or replace a lost charger. The compact size keeps drills light.

For long jobs buy a 4.0Ah pack or more. This one is for light use and spares. Treat it as a starter pack, and add a 4.0Ah or larger pack once you buy a saw or blower, since the ONE+ platform makes it easy to add capacity.
products.bestFor: Beginners starting ONE+ or buying a light spare.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A battery is a ticket into a tool family. Milwaukee M18 covers over 60 tools in the listing quoted, Makita LXT covers hundreds, and Ryobi ONE+ covers over 225. Choose the platform that has the tools you will buy next, since packs do not cross brands. Look at the tools you want in five years, not only the one you buy today.

Capacity sets runtime. A 2.0Ah pack stores about 36 watt-hours, a 4.0Ah pack about 72 and a 5.0Ah pack about 90 at 18 volts nominal. Pick 2 to 4Ah for drills and 5Ah or more for saws and grinders. Bigger packs weigh more. Always check capacity against tool weight before you commit.

The Milwaukee REDLINK system links tool, pack and charger to protect against overload. Makita packs communicate with their chargers to optimize charging. Smarter packs last longer and protect tools. Cheap third-party packs usually lack this. Cheap packs usually lack the communication chip that protects your tool.

An onboard gauge, as on the Milwaukee 48-11-1850, shows how much runtime remains, and an LED indicator on the Makita BL1850B does the same in steps. Without a gauge you only find out when the tool stops. A gauge saves you from running dry in the middle of a cut.

Makita lists 45 minutes or less for a 5.0Ah pack on a rapid charger, and Ryobi lists under one hour for its 2.0Ah kit. Charge time depends on the charger. A fast charger lets one pack cover a day. A fast charger is an easy way to double the working time of one pack.

The Milwaukee XC5.0 Resistant has a housing designed to resist oils and chemicals. Shops and trucks are hard on packs. A tough shell prevents cracks and contact damage. If you work around oil, the resistant housing pays for itself.

specDecoder.meaning: 18 volt is the nominal voltage of five lithium cells in series. Under no load a fully charged pack reads about 20 volts. It is the figure to compare before you look at any price.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 20V MAX tool and an 18V tool are the same voltage class but from different makers.

specDecoder.meaning: Amp-hours measure how much charge a pack holds. Multiply by voltage to get watt-hours. It is the figure to compare before you look at any price.
specDecoder.watchFor: Capacity does not describe power delivery.

specDecoder.meaning: Watt-hours measure energy. A 5.0Ah 18V pack holds about 90 Wh. It is the figure to compare before you look at any price.
specDecoder.watchFor: Compare Wh when comparing packs of different voltages.

specDecoder.meaning: High output or High Performance packs use cells that deliver more current. They help brushless saws and grinders. It is the figure to compare before you look at any price.
specDecoder.watchFor: Power claims compare against the maker's own older packs.

specDecoder.meaning: Extended capacity, as in XC, means more cells or higher-capacity cells. It adds runtime and weight. It is the figure to compare before you look at any price.

maintenance.why: Cells age faster at 100 percent or empty. Store around 40 to 60 percent. It costs nothing and extends the life of the pack.
Heat shortens life. Do not leave them in a hot truck. It costs nothing and extends the life of the pack.
Dirty contacts cause poor connection. Wipe them dry. It costs nothing and extends the life of the pack.
Alternate packs so they age evenly. It costs nothing and extends the life of the pack.
A swollen or cracked pack is a hazard. Retire it. It costs nothing and extends the life of the pack.

faq.a: They are the same voltage class, but a brand's pack only fits its own tools. 20V MAX is a marketing label. Check the connector and brand name, not only the voltage.

faq.q: Which platform should I buy into?
faq.a: Choose the one with the tools you will want. Ryobi is broad for homes, and Milwaukee and Makita are strong for trades. Think about which tools you will buy in the next two years, since the battery is the expensive part.
It gives longer runtime but adds weight. Match capacity to the tool. A 5.0Ah pack on a small drill is just a heavier battery, so choose by tool.
Many last several years or hundreds of cycles. Heat and deep discharge shorten life. Storing at partial charge in a cool room doubles useful life compared with leaving packs in a hot truck.
Some work, but many overstate capacity and lack protection. Genuine packs are safer. Check that the seller is authorized and that the pack carries the maker's marks.

faq.q: Can I use a 5.0Ah battery where a 2.0Ah fits?
faq.a: Yes, it fits the same slot. The tool just runs longer. It fits, and the tool will simply run longer between charges.
